summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated payload
details: @onereach/si-merge-tag-input@0.4.6 advertises itself as a Vue merge-tag input component but ships a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases at install time, unzips it, chmods it executable, and uses it to execute a bundled 727KB heavily obfuscated file `math_init.js` (obfuscator.io fingerprints: rotated string array via `WV8StW`, hex-named globals, large hex-encoded constant table). `setup.mjs` itself is obfuscated with the same toolchain (`_0xNNNN` proxy-object indirection). A Vue input component has no legitimate need for a second JavaScript runtime or an opaque `math_init` payload; executing the payload under Bun instead of Node evades standard Node-based static analysis. On `npm install`, this results in execution of attacker-controlled, obfuscated code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
